episode_thesis: Pablo Calderini (Graham Capital macro PM) presents a client talk arguing that macro adds value to equity-heavy portfolios because it has conditional low-to-negative correlation to equities and bonds: it follows central-bank policy and changes direction by regime. He explains why 2010-2020 starved macro (the central-bank put suppressed volatility), why the 2022 inflation shock changed that, and why mid-2024 calm (low VIX, MOVE and FX vol) sits against large tail risks (inflation rebound, China-Taiwan, Middle East) and a positive stock-bond correlation. Adding 10-20% macro to a 60/40 portfolio since 1990 raised return, cut volatility, lifted Sharpe and shrank drawdown.

speakers.name: Pablo Calderini
speakers.role: Macro portfolio manager, Graham Capital Management (presenting to clients)
speakers.speaker_note: Single-speaker presentation from Whisper speech-to-text; he refers to slides ('this chart here'), so some chart values are inferred from his narration. Ledger correction applied to C01-3: the S&P rose about 1000 points from a late-October 2023 low near 4200, and the rally began before the Fed's December dovish pivot (markets anticipated it). 'Information ratio' is used for the Sharpe-type ratio. Recording is dated 2024-06-03 and refers to April 2024 events, so views carry as_of 2024-05/06.

worldview_premises.premise: From 2010 to 2020 the central-bank put turned bad news into higher asset prices, compressing volatility, which was a great time for asset owners and a difficult one for macro traders.
worldview_premises.support: Narrative of GFC aftermath; low volatility in the period.

worldview_premises.premise: Loose monetary and fiscal policy after COVID led to asset inflation and then the 2022 inflation shock, which broke the central-bank put: banks had to tighten rather than ease, in the fastest hike cycle outside Volcker with the largest real-rate rise.
worldview_premises.support: Fed funds from 0-0.25% to 5.25-5.5%; PCE monthly prints (headline 1.2% in a month, 15% annualised; core about 8% annualised).

worldview_premises.premise: Macro performs best when central banks are actively changing policy because central-bank policy is the input a macro book can anticipate; growth, inflation and the Fed are the main inputs, along with any micro story that moves global markets (for example Nvidia as an AI proxy).
worldview_premises.support: Own record in 2022; no formal test.

worldview_premises.premise: The stock-bond correlation is bimodal over 100 years (zero on average, almost never near zero): positive in 1960-1995 and negative in the last 20 years. It is negative when growth shocks dominate (rates fall on bad news) and positive when inflation is high (bad news hits both).
Macro is a dynamic strategy with no long or short bias: it goes long equities in good markets and cuts or shorts them in bad ones, so correlation is conditional rather than reliably negative.
worldview_premises.support: Rolling-correlation chart of the macro index versus MSCI World; drawdown table.

worldview_premises.premise: Macro is not a guaranteed hedge: a fast shock (Q1 2020) can find the book unready and cost money, unlike buying equity puts.
Very low volatility with elevated geopolitical and inflation tail risk leaves equities exposed to large corrections after strong rallies.
worldview_premises.support: Straight-line Q1 2024 equity rally with a Sharpe-type ratio near 4; low VIX, MOVE and FX vol.

worldview_premises.premise: Climate-driven weather extremes can produce large commodity moves (cocoa up four times or more).
worldview_premises.support: Cocoa price chart; anecdotes about snow and West African rain and drought.

mechanism_chains.topic: Why macro profited in 2022 and what it held

steps.to: central banks cannot ease and must tighten by 400-500bp
stocks and commodities fall; dollar rises as the Fed is the most aggressive
steps.why: usual effect of heavy tightening; relative policy stance

steps.from: positioned short rates, short stocks, short commodities, long USD
steps.to: macro index about +10% while equities fell 25%

mechanism_chains.evidence: 2022 numbers: MSCI World down 25%; macro index up about 10%; Graham's program more than double.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Central banks on hold or positions mistimed; in Q1 2020 a fast shock hurt.

mechanism_chains.topic: Stock-bond correlation, inflation and the failing 60/40

steps.to: rates fall on bad growth news; stocks and bonds move opposite

steps.from: inflation high or a hot inflation print
steps.to: stocks and bonds fall together (positive correlation)
worse diversification for 60/40 owners, depends on inflation path

mechanism_chains.fails_when: Inflation falls and growth shocks dominate again.

mechanism_chains.topic: 2024 equity rally and the left tail

steps.from: Fed and every developed central bank except the BoJ turn dovish with decent growth (Dec 2023), anticipated by markets
steps.to: S&P up about 1000 points in four months with very low volatility

steps.from: a big rally with low vol
steps.to: left tail if a shock hits (core PCE at 5% annualised forcing another hike, a China-Taiwan crisis, Middle East escalation)
steps.why: markets can retrace 1000 points as easily

mechanism_chains.evidence: Chart of the S&P, VIX, MOVE and JPM FX vol; PCE series.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Earnings keep rising and inflation continues down; he notes AI profits are real unlike the 2002 internet.

mechanism_chains.topic: How adding macro improves a 60/40 portfolio

steps.from: macro index has lower volatility than equities and almost zero correlation to the portfolio
lower volatility with similar or higher return
steps.to: higher Sharpe ratio and smaller drawdown, lower equity beta

mechanism_chains.evidence: 1990 to December 2023: adding 20% macro raised return from 6.7% to 7.2%, cut volatility from 10.2% to 8.7%, lifted Sharpe from 0.65 to 0.83, cut max drawdown from 36% to 29% and beta from 0.7 to 0.55.
mechanism_chains.fails_when: Macro correlation rises or macro fails in a fast shock.

decision_process.practice: Forecast growth, inflation and central-bank policy; trade directional and relative positions across rates, equities, commodities and FX, and change equity exposure by regime.
decision_process.why: Central-bank action is the most anticipatable input.

decision_process.practice: Take no standing long or short equity bias; get short in anticipation of and during bad equity markets and long in good ones.
decision_process.why: Dynamic exposure produces negative conditional correlation without buying puts.

decision_process.practice: Watch anything that moves global markets, including single-stock stories that become macro (Nvidia).
Conviction is scaled by regime: lower in 2024 than 2022 though still short rates, with US curve steepeners, short Japanese rates and long dollar.
Position macro between passive/long-only tactical allocation and pure arbitrage: low long-run correlation but active directional exposure.
Recommend investors allocate 10-20% of a 60/40 portfolio to macro.
decision_process.why: Backtested improvement in returns, volatility, Sharpe and drawdown.

decision_process.practice: Follow core PCE, the Fed's target series, rather than headline PCE.

speakers.evidence_style: Presentation-based historical statistics and charts: drawdown table (1990, 2000-02, 2008, 2022), century stock-bond correlation, portfolio-with-macro numbers 1990-2023, volatility indices, PCE data. Manager-specific claims come from a firm presentation, with the macro index as the comparator.

current_views.view: Inflation is the biggest shock; core PCE prints annualising near 5% would force another Fed hike. It is a main tail risk, not the base case.
current_views.reasoning: Inflation has bounced back off its lows to levels not consistent with 2%.

current_views.view: Stay short rates (US steepeners, short Japan) and long the dollar, with less conviction than in 2022.
current_views.reasoning: Strong US economy limits Fed cuts while the ECB is about to cut independently; Japanese rates should rise a lot.

current_views.view: Equity valuations are not a complete concern since earnings and AI profits are growing, but a shock could retrace the 1000-point rally.
current_views.reasoning: Part P/E expansion, part earnings; AI firms make real profits.

current_views.view: Volatility is low (VIX about 16 after 13, MOVE about 100, FX vol low) while geopolitical risk is the highest since WWII: a China-Taiwan blockade or invasion would be the largest financial shock ever.
current_views.reasoning: Low vol is at odds with tail risks.

current_views.view: The April Iran-Israel exchange was largely symbolic and a short-term truce, but a line was crossed and escalation by miscalculation remains possible; Ukraine is far from settled.
current_views.reasoning: Attacks were staged for domestic audiences; one mass-casualty strike would have prompted a harder response.

current_views.view: Stock-bond correlation is positive again, bad for 60/40 owners, and depends on the inflation path.
Climate-driven weather extremes (cocoa quadrupled) may foreshadow commodity volatility, though not currently a concern for trading.
Central banks (all except the BoJ) turned dovish in December 2023 into a decent-growth backdrop, which markets had anticipated.

gaps_and_conflicts.issue: He says the macro index averaged 'up 10%' in 2022 and Graham's program 'more than double', a manager-specific claim from a firm presentation; the index is not named and the 1990 and 2000-02 figures are also from the same source (2008 stated only as 'positive').

Macro is not a guaranteed hedge (Q1 2020 -2%) yet the sales case stresses drawdown protection across four episodes; sample is selected to show wins and there is no distribution of conditional returns.
Portfolio effect (1990-2023) uses a macro index, not Graham's own track record, so the 6.7-to-7.2% and 0.65-to-0.83 figures cannot be attributed to Graham; no costs or fee treatment given.
Skill at forecasting bad equity markets is self-reported; the correlation chart is described qualitatively ('does a really good job') with no tracking statistic.
Captions say 'average correlation is zero, 400 years' and 'roll down' for drawdown, which look like transcription errors for 100 years and drawdown; the ledger reads 100 years.
Equity valuations are not a concern because earnings are growing, yet he also warns that a 1000-point rally can unwind quickly; both statements rely on the shock case.

forward_looking_inputs: (reader) Core PCE monthly prints and annualised pace, Fed reaction (hike risk), the stock-bond correlation sign, VIX, MOVE and FX vol levels versus geopolitical events (Taiwan, Middle East, Ukraine), US growth strength relative to Europe (ECB independent cuts), Japanese rate path. Horizon: months for inflation and policy, with tail risks undated.
reader_inferences: (reader) The central logic is regime dependence: macro does well when central banks act and when inflation prevents the central-bank put; in a put regime it is starved.
(reader) The sales case rests on dynamic exposure rather than convexity; he states explicitly that macro is not an equity put.
(reader) Compared with MT066, MT089, MT090 and MT214 (all Graham, Tropin), the same volatility-supply thesis appears with added stock-bond correlation and portfolio-construction evidence.
